hook_text: Ancient Egypt built pyramids of stone, and its society was a pyramid too.
clip_script: East London, Eastern Cape. A giant paper pyramid on the wall. At the top: one pharaoh, believed to be a god on Earth. Below: the vizier, nobles and priests. Then scribes, who could read and write, and soldiers. Then craftspeople and traders. And at the wide bottom: farmers, the biggest group of all, who fed everyone and paid taxes. Women could own property, and Hatshepsut ruled as pharaoh.
visual_style: Whiteboard pyramid filling layer by layer with little figures, from one pharaoh at the top to many farmers at the base.
mood: Curious and clear, like building something together.
pacing: Top to bottom, one layer at a time.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw your own social pyramid of ancient Egypt.
